briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Tax Relief Gains Bipartisan Ground in Michigan as Rescheduling and Psychedelics Momentum Builds Nationally
briefs.top: Michigan's 24% wholesale tax is still squeezing margins, but political momentum for repeal just went bipartisan and the state Supreme Court handed operators a real civil-liberties win. Nationally, DEA's own rescheduling case is now public record, psychedelics are racing toward FDA approval, and Curaleaf's bid for Aurora shows real capital chasing cannabis growth again.

local.text: A Michigan cannabis company confirmed it's shuttering five of its nine dispensaries, citing the state's 24% wholesale tax; <cite index="1-3">Higher Love Cannabis Co.'s Upper Peninsula stores in Crystal Falls, Escanaba, Houghton, Munising, and Ontonagon closed for good on August 9.</cite> The pullback thins out an oversaturated UP market, opening real runway for surviving retailers to absorb the freed-up customer base.

<cite index="46-1">GOP gubernatorial nominee John James is pledging to repeal or sharply cut the 24% wholesale tax as part of a cannabis policy platform he unveiled August 19.</cite> With Democratic contenders also on record opposing the levy, operators now have bipartisan momentum heading into a governor's race that could finally deliver tax relief.

<cite index="4-1">Michigan's Supreme Court just rewrote the rules governing marijuana-related searches</cite>, tightening the constitutional bar police must clear before treating legal product as probable cause. It's a meaningful win for licensed operators and customers tired of being treated like suspects for buying something legal.

The industry's legal fight for relief is still very much alive: <cite index="54-2,54-3">the Michigan Cannabis Industry Association filed a second constitutional lawsuit arguing the 24% wholesale tax creates an unconstitutional tax-on-tax spiral that pushes the effective rate above the 6% ceiling voters set in 2018.</cite> A win would retroactively unwind one of the industry's biggest cost burdens.

Even amid the tax squeeze, demand keeps climbing: <cite index="42-8,42-9">Michigan dispensaries moved nearly 104,000 pounds of adult-use flower in January 2026, the highest volume for that month in the program's six-year history, with average prices near an all-time low of $59.07 an ounce.</cite> Volume like that is the clearest signal yet the market can outgrow its pricing pain.

national.text: <cite index="18-6">The DEA released the full official transcript of its cannabis rescheduling hearing, showing government lawyers arguing marijuana "can no longer remain in Schedule I."</cite> The public record now backs what operators have argued for years — and puts fresh pressure on regulators to finish the job.

<cite index="26-3">Lykos, now rebranded Resilient Pharmaceuticals, resubmitted its MDMA therapy NDA in August 2026 under the proposed brand name Rysanso</cite>, <cite index="26-4">adding a third-party audit of the original trials, a new cardiac-safety study, and VA follow-up data to address the FDA's prior rejection.</cite> It's a real second shot at the first approved MDMA-assisted therapy.

<cite index="24-4">The FDA announced a September 14, 2026 public hearing to gather feedback on the future therapeutic use of psychedelic drugs</cite>, right after finalizing formal clinical-trial guidance for the category. <cite index="22-7">Compass Pathways is targeting a Q4 2026 NDA filing for its COMP360 psilocybin treatment</cite>, putting a classic psychedelic within sight of the U.S. market.

<cite index="22-5,22-6">The VA launched PIVOT, a five-site clinical trial testing Compass Pathways' COMP360 psilocybin for veterans with treatment-resistant depression, starting August 5.</cite> Federal buy-in from the VA is a major credibility signal for psychedelic medicine heading into next year's approval decisions.

<cite index="58-4">Curaleaf confirmed plans to acquire all of Aurora Cannabis in a stock-and-cash deal</cite>, though <cite index="61-5">Aurora has urged shareholders to take no action on the offer</cite> as the fight plays out. Contested or not, it's the clearest sign yet that rescheduling optimism is fueling a real cannabis M&A wave.
